pr_comments:
@allevo It can't be a plugin, because in this way it would be called too late. And, for example, in logs you'll not see what's expected.

Probably it could be implemented like a plugin, but then I think it will need to move logging to separate plugin as well. Or moving logs function call triggers at least after `onRequest` hook. In this case trustProxy could be implemented like a plugin that just adds a hook.

I agree with @allevo, we should be able to expose this as a plugin.
The main idea around Fastify is to be *future proof* the more we can delegate to plugins the better.
The core should be as light as possible, if we need to expose a new API to enable better plugins, that's the way!
@allevo In this case I don't see reasons why logger is part of the core. Making it (logger) as plugin will allow to configure it accordingly without overrides.
@mcollina Sorry, unfortunately currently I have no time to finish this up.
This pull request has been automatically locked since there has not been any recent activity after it was closed. Please open a new issue for related bugs.

issue_context.title: Enable trust proxy?
issue_context.body:
Hello.

How can I enable trust proxy to get the ip with x-forwarded-for like in Express.js?
comments: Can you please explain this with a bit more detail? What code are you trying to port?
I'm not trying to port something. Express has a function to enable trust proxy and with that I can get the person's ip address using req.ip. Is this possible in fastify?
No it does not. It should be trivial to add.
I do want to say that when enabling trust proxy without running the app behind a proxy like nginx, the header x-forwarded-for can be spoofed. Express disables trust proxy by default.

@Zaseth definitely. I think we should add a `trustProxy` option to fastify and use https://www.npmjs.com/package/proxy-addr in a similar way to how express uses it. 

Some pointers: https://github.com/expressjs/express/blob/b97faff6e2aa4d34d79485fe4331cb0eec13ad57/lib/request.js#L292-L324 https://github.com/expressjs/express/blob/c0136d8b48dd3526c58b2ad8666fb4b12b55116c/lib/utils.js#L212-L239
This could be a very useful feature. There should be a note for the proper configuration for the nginx config when using this feature, but I assume that you already know about this.

review_comments:
I think is better to add all these properties to our [`Request`](https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/master/lib/request.js) object, instead of decorating the Node core one. We should change the Node core object only if is really necessary and I don't think this is the case.

The logger serializer should be updated accordingly.
We can't do differently in a semver-minor. We are currently setting the logger on the node core request object as we still do not have our Request allocated. We could do the reverse in v2.
Can you use a truthy check?
